memory_candidates.content: git log -S'<literal>' --oneline on a JSON state file can mislead on attribution: -S matches any commit that changes the occurrence COUNT of a string, including commits that only REMOVE/relocate it (e.g. archiving entries away). To find the true introducing commit, diff each candidate commit's before/after content with jq (presence+value check) rather than trusting which commits the pickaxe search surfaces or trusting a prior commit message's own attribution.

In BimodalLogic's validate-state.sh, promoting one WARN-level sub-state of a multi-sub-state check to FAIL (while others stay WARN) requires splitting both the per-finding log call (branch per sub_state) AND the aggregate summary line (which otherwise blends all sub-states into one log_warn and would misclassify an unrelated sub-state's findings as FAIL). A single promoted sub-state needs its own conditionally-emitted summary line, not a wholesale re-level of the existing one.
